input.prompt:
Paint one production-ready 1536x1024 map floor atlas for element 17033, with exactly three columns and two rows. Each cell is a complete 512x512 opaque edge-to-edge square tile, placed flush without any gutters, empty background, framing, or labels. Each of the six images fills its own exact square. The camera is perfectly top-down and orthographic throughout. The stone frame and internal metal mesh belong to the tile, not the surroundings. Keep the outer silhouette an exact full square including all four corners.

Image 1 is the real 6-phase source contact sheet. It is the authority for rail orientation, phase sequence, proportions, and locations of moving solid plates relative to the checker-like perforated mesh. Treat every source frame independently in row-major order. The checker-like texture is physical iron mesh above a dark opaque backing. Image 2 is our existing original frame-0 art for this exact element, used as identity and material reference. The primary outer frame and curved rail follow the TOP and RIGHT edges, with the curved arc bending around the upper-right corner. Pivot/cutout detail at BOTTOM LEFT. Image 3 is our already painted sibling material atlas. Match the same charcoal stone and dark iron mesh shading and restrained thin warm-brass edging, but ignore the sister tile's corner placement and phase order. Images 4 and 5 are original Daoist chibi hand-painted finish references only. No figures, UI, typography or additional jade ornament.

Retain exactly the rail, taper and plate proportions of Image 1, corresponding to our original finish in Image 2. The outer rail stays pinned to those same edges in all cells. Subtle rail joint position can change to match the exact source frame, and the dark outlined solid grey sector or sectors sweep over the fine opaque mesh. Each edge between smooth solid graphite plate and the tiny tightly repeated metal grid has a crisp readable contour. Copy the structure, not pixels. Small broad color and lighting differences between states are allowed only to make the moving panel distinguishable. No gold ornament inside the track, no light-up arrows, no added handle or bolts, no literal opening or transparent hole.

Frame 0: solid wedge on the upper-left/left half, open mesh lower right. Frame 1: solid wedge center-right with mesh upper left and lower right. Frame 2: solid wedge shifts toward lower-right with a broader mesh triangle above-left. Frame 3: open mesh triangle at upper center-right and separate narrow solid left strip plus broad solid bottom-right region. Frame 4: upper mesh triangle widens toward center with solid bottom-right sector, a dark thin mesh strip below. Frame 5: mesh wedge rotated more steeply to occupy center-right, broad solid left and a lower-right solid strip.
Top row left to right is 0, 1, 2. Bottom row left to right is 3, 4, 5. Follow the corresponding source panel angle and mesh-versus-solid divisions, retaining the fixed rail orientation and full edge-to-edge square. High-definition hand-painted game art, texture and material realism compatible with our Daoist Q world. No independent sheets, no white matte, no perspective, no shadows beyond the tile, no sticker outline, no checkerboard background, no captions.
